# Invoke a custom operation

Register your own Web Services operation in Vtiger, then call it with `invokeOperation()`.

## Register the operation in Vtiger

```sql
INSERT INTO `vtiger_ws_operation`
       (`name`, `handler_path`, `handler_method`, `type`, `prelogin`)
VALUES ('new_operation', 'include/Webservices/MyCoolWebService.php', 'new_operation_method', 'PUT', 0);

-- Replace <new_operation_ID> with the actual ID generated by the query above
INSERT INTO `vtiger_ws_operation_parameters` (`operationid`, `name`, `type`, `sequence`)
VALUES (<new_operation_ID>, 'someParam', 'String', 1);

INSERT INTO `vtiger_ws_operation_parameters` (`operationid`, `name`, `type`, `sequence`)
VALUES (<new_operation_ID>, 'dateParam', 'TimeStamp ', 2);
```

Then create `include/Webservices/MyCoolWebService.php` in the Vtiger installation:

```php
<?php

function new_operation_method($someParam, $dateParam){
    global $log, $adb;

    // ... do something here

    return $result;
}
```

## Call it

```php
$result = $client->invokeOperation('new_operation', [
    'someParam' => 'foobar',
    'dateParam' => strtotime('now'),
], 'POST');
```

`invokeOperation()` takes the operation name, an associative array of parameters, and the HTTP method (default `POST`). A list-style parameter array throws `VtWsClientException`. See the [`VtWsClient` reference](../tools/vtwsclient.md).
